7 Comments

Join the conversation
Sign in to read what others are saying and share your thoughts.Ado (アド) is a female utaite who began her activities on January 10, 2017 at the age of 14 with a cover of KuwagataP's Kimi no Taion in her second year of middle school.[3][4] She picked it because it was stylish and cool.[5] She started singing because of VOCALOID after learning about it from her cousin[5][6][7] at around 1st grade[8] when she was 5 or 6 years old[9], thanks to Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin, and Kagamine Len rather than a specific producer[4][10][11] and series like Jin's Kagerou Project[5], which was having an anime adaptation at her age.[3] She learned about utattemita in her 6th[5] grade of elementary school[12], thanks to fellow utaite like Mafumafu[3][5][10][13], Soraru[3][5][10][13], Amatsuki[3][5], Rib[3][5][10][13], Wolpis Carter[5][13], 96Neko[5], Itou Kashitarou[5][13], Megatera Zero[13] and many more. One of the reasons Ado became popular was the song Shikabaneeze  (Corpsese), created by VOCALOID producer jon-YAKITORY. He gave her an offer to do an official cover for it in June 2020 when she was 17, and she accepted, to which it became a sensation on TikTok and subscription services.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

7 Comments

Join the conversation
Sign in to read what others are saying and share your thoughts.Ado (アド) is a female utaite who began her activities on January 10, 2017 at the age of 14 with a cover of KuwagataP's Kimi no Taion in her second year of middle school.[3][4] She picked it because it was stylish and cool.[5] She started singing because of VOCALOID after learning about it from her cousin[5][6][7] at around 1st grade[8] when she was 5 or 6 years old[9], thanks to Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin, and Kagamine Len rather than a specific producer[4][10][11] and series like Jin's Kagerou Project[5], which was having an anime adaptation at her age.[3] She learned about utattemita in her 6th[5] grade of elementary school[12], thanks to fellow utaite like Mafumafu[3][5][10][13], Soraru[3][5][10][13], Amatsuki[3][5], Rib[3][5][10][13], Wolpis Carter[5][13], 96Neko[5], Itou Kashitarou[5][13], Megatera Zero[13] and many more. One of the reasons Ado became popular was the song Shikabaneeze  (Corpsese), created by VOCALOID producer jon-YAKITORY. He gave her an offer to do an official cover for it in June 2020 when she was 17, and she accepted, to which it became a sensation on TikTok and subscription services.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

Join the conversation
Sign in to read what others are saying and share your thoughts.Ado (アド) is a female utaite who began her activities on January 10, 2017 at the age of 14 with a cover of KuwagataP's Kimi no Taion in her second year of middle school.[3][4] She picked it because it was stylish and cool.[5] She started singing because of VOCALOID after learning about it from her cousin[5][6][7] at around 1st grade[8] when she was 5 or 6 years old[9], thanks to Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin, and Kagamine Len rather than a specific producer[4][10][11] and series like Jin's Kagerou Project[5], which was having an anime adaptation at her age.[3] She learned about utattemita in her 6th[5] grade of elementary school[12], thanks to fellow utaite like Mafumafu[3][5][10][13], Soraru[3][5][10][13], Amatsuki[3][5], Rib[3][5][10][13], Wolpis Carter[5][13], 96Neko[5], Itou Kashitarou[5][13], Megatera Zero[13] and many more. One of the reasons Ado became popular was the song Shikabaneeze  (Corpsese), created by VOCALOID producer jon-YAKITORY. He gave her an offer to do an official cover for it in June 2020 when she was 17, and she accepted, to which it became a sensation on TikTok and subscription services.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

Sign in to read what others are saying and share your thoughts.Ado (アド) is a female utaite who began her activities on January 10, 2017 at the age of 14 with a cover of KuwagataP's Kimi no Taion in her second year of middle school.[3][4] She picked it because it was stylish and cool.[5] She started singing because of VOCALOID after learning about it from her cousin[5][6][7] at around 1st grade[8] when she was 5 or 6 years old[9], thanks to Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin, and Kagamine Len rather than a specific producer[4][10][11] and series like Jin's Kagerou Project[5], which was having an anime adaptation at her age.[3] She learned about utattemita in her 6th[5] grade of elementary school[12], thanks to fellow utaite like Mafumafu[3][5][10][13], Soraru[3][5][10][13], Amatsuki[3][5], Rib[3][5][10][13], Wolpis Carter[5][13], 96Neko[5], Itou Kashitarou[5][13], Megatera Zero[13] and many more. One of the reasons Ado became popular was the song Shikabaneeze  (Corpsese), created by VOCALOID producer jon-YAKITORY. He gave her an offer to do an official cover for it in June 2020 when she was 17, and she accepted, to which it became a sensation on TikTok and subscription services.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

Sign in to read what others are saying and share your thoughts.Ado (アド) is a female utaite who began her activities on January 10, 2017 at the age of 14 with a cover of KuwagataP's Kimi no Taion in her second year of middle school.[3][4] She picked it because it was stylish and cool.[5] She started singing because of VOCALOID after learning about it from her cousin[5][6][7] at around 1st grade[8] when she was 5 or 6 years old[9], thanks to Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin, and Kagamine Len rather than a specific producer[4][10][11] and series like Jin's Kagerou Project[5], which was having an anime adaptation at her age.[3] She learned about utattemita in her 6th[5] grade of elementary school[12], thanks to fellow utaite like Mafumafu[3][5][10][13], Soraru[3][5][10][13], Amatsuki[3][5], Rib[3][5][10][13], Wolpis Carter[5][13], 96Neko[5], Itou Kashitarou[5][13], Megatera Zero[13] and many more. One of the reasons Ado became popular was the song Shikabaneeze  (Corpsese), created by VOCALOID producer jon-YAKITORY. He gave her an offer to do an official cover for it in June 2020 when she was 17, and she accepted, to which it became a sensation on TikTok and subscription services.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

Sign in to read what others are saying and share your thoughts.Ado (アド) is a female utaite who began her activities on January 10, 2017 at the age of 14 with a cover of KuwagataP's Kimi no Taion in her second year of middle school.[3][4] She picked it because it was stylish and cool.[5] She started singing because of VOCALOID after learning about it from her cousin[5][6][7] at around 1st grade[8] when she was 5 or 6 years old[9], thanks to Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin, and Kagamine Len rather than a specific producer[4][10][11] and series like Jin's Kagerou Project[5], which was having an anime adaptation at her age.[3] She learned about utattemita in her 6th[5] grade of elementary school[12], thanks to fellow utaite like Mafumafu[3][5][10][13], Soraru[3][5][10][13], Amatsuki[3][5], Rib[3][5][10][13], Wolpis Carter[5][13], 96Neko[5], Itou Kashitarou[5][13], Megatera Zero[13] and many more. One of the reasons Ado became popular was the song Shikabaneeze  (Corpsese), created by VOCALOID producer jon-YAKITORY. He gave her an offer to do an official cover for it in June 2020 when she was 17, and she accepted, to which it became a sensation on TikTok and subscription services.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]

7 Comments

Join the conversation
Sign in to read what others are saying and share your thoughts.Ado (アド) is a female utaite who began her activities on January 10, 2017 at the age of 14 with a cover of KuwagataP's Kimi no Taion in her second year of middle school.[3][4] She picked it because it was stylish and cool.[5] She started singing because of VOCALOID after learning about it from her cousin[5][6][7] at around 1st grade[8] when she was 5 or 6 years old[9], thanks to Hatsune Miku, Kagamine Rin, and Kagamine Len rather than a specific producer[4][10][11] and series like Jin's Kagerou Project[5], which was having an anime adaptation at her age.[3] She learned about utattemita in her 6th[5] grade of elementary school[12], thanks to fellow utaite like Mafumafu[3][5][10][13], Soraru[3][5][10][13], Amatsuki[3][5], Rib[3][5][10][13], Wolpis Carter[5][13], 96Neko[5], Itou Kashitarou[5][13], Megatera Zero[13] and many more. One of the reasons Ado became popular was the song Shikabaneeze  (Corpsese), created by VOCALOID producer jon-YAKITORY. He gave her an offer to do an official cover for it in June 2020 when she was 17, and she accepted, to which it became a sensation on TikTok and subscription services.[3]

In October the same year, she then made her largest explosion onto the music scene with her debut release of "Usseewa"  , signed to Universal Music Japan under Virgin Music's Cloud Nine label.[14] After Usseewa went viral, her wishes for the near future was to keep singing and have a concert.[12] Indeed, she held her first one-man live on the 10th of January, 2021, at Zepp Divercity.[15] Her fellow utaite, and main collaboration partners, Yoshino and Jyakusansei, are also under Cloud Nine.[16] As of July 2025, Usseewa has over 383 million views on YouTube, and over 256 million plays on Spotify. Since then, Ado has been garnering lots of attention when releasing new covers or original music and she also releases albums of her covered songs as well.

From the release of big-hit singles like "Show"  to the globetrotting "Uta no Uta" One Piece: Film RED soundtrack/album (where she showed her range in regular pop ("Shin Jidai" , "Watashi wa saikyo" ), heart breaking and warming ballads ("Sekai no Tsuzuki" , "Kaze no Yukue" ), furious rock ("Gyakko" , "Tot Musica" ), and even energetic hip-hop ("Utakata Lullaby" ) and a sea shanty ("Binkusu no Sake" )!), Ado has only risen since her smash hit Usseewa . She has even made her debut in the United States, having signed to Geffen Records on her 20th birthday in 2022[17] and embarking on a world tour at 21[18], yet even as a global artist she still does utattemita, making her beloved by many.

Her most popular cover on Nico Nico Douga is her cover of syudou's Jama  with over 2.6 million views, while on Youtube it is of PinocchioP's God-ish  with over 51 million views as of July 2025.

Ado has always had a darker tone compared to your average female singer, like in her cover of Strangers , where although her voice was light as she was still a teenager, it still had the distinctive rasp of the Ado we know today. At the same time, she was always good at being able to reach high notes, such as the way she utilized her head voice in her cover of Star Night Snow . In classical music terms, she is a mezzo-soprano.[19] According to herself, a turning point in the development of her voice was her cover of Wada Takeaki's Kirai Kirai Jiga Hidai! as her using more growls gave her more reactions, so she knew she could sing stronger[4] and felt it was part of her style.[20] She said that it was the first time that she started using different vocal techniques like shouting while singing and raising her voice, which she felt was very fitting for her. She felt that she had really gotten the hang of singing by then.[5]

As Ado has matured, she now has a versatile voice and is able to add power to it. Her vocals, with a dark and cool timbre, usually give off an angsty vibe as of a rebellious teenager, which have now become a signature part of her style, especially in some of her original and cover songs like "Readymade"  and Tsumi to Batsu , where she best utilizes it. She uses growls to inject a gravelly angst into her voice, but can also belt a soft and clear falsetto on a dime. Not only that, her vocal range itself aside from her techniques is astounding; displayed in Aishite Aishite Aishite  to its fullest extent (C3-G♯6[19]), Ado's latest measure of vocal range is from a low and rumbling fried G♯2[Note 1][19], banging all the way up through to an ear-piercing screamed C♯7[Note 2][19] (in total, 4 octaves and 5 semitones[19]).

Simply put, Ado's way of growling, voice-acted like tones, and reaching high notes as well as singing soft and sweet, all within the same song, makes her unique. She also often uses her voice to reach nearly surreal heights in order to accompany the emotion within her way of singing.

Trivia
Ado had the equipment to start singing since 6th grade, but since she was slow to pick things up, she didn't know how to actually use it to record. She managed to finally finish a video while she was in middle school.[3]
The name for Ado's representative character is Chando (チャンド), taken from what some people call her, "Ado-chan" (Adoちゃん).[21]
She is 157cm tall. Chando is 163cm tall.[22]
She is known for her secretiveness. In her early days, rumors were that she was some kind of highly advanced VOCALOID voicebank[citation needed], she never reveals her face (with the video for the piano version of Usseewa being the closest), and her handshake event has her shake fans hands through a box. She has not told anyone that she is Ado, even her classmates or anyone else, except her close friends.[12] This has caused an issue at Geino shrine where she couldn't put up a plaque for herself due to having to provide "proof" of her identity, which she didn't have on her at the time (not even her manager's card) and she worried that just showing her social media or singing on the spot would lead people to think she was a fake. [23]
On Niconico, most of her covers' titles would have a pun that had something to do with her name "Ado". For example, Adovance , Adorably , Adoventure , Adovice , and Adornment .
In her earlier stages of singing covers, she sung in a closet[12], which she made by trying to stick sound-absorbing materials and other materials to it.[10]. She has said that she thought it was a great space for soundproofing.
Her name "Ado" originates from the term for the supporting actor of traditional Japanese comic theatre Kyogen, which she decided after she studied the play Kaki Yamabushi (The Persimmon Thief) in elementary school.[24] She chose to name herself after this instead of the main actor "Shite" because her wish was to be a supporting character in someone's life through song[4][10] (see her Artist on the Rise video ).
The blue rose often if not always displayed in her general media represents flower language. After finally being genetically-engineered by Japanese researchers in 2002, its flower language was changed from "impossible" to "dreams coming true".[25][26] It's a term that resonates with Ado's personality, as well as her dream of one day singing live for a large audience coming true.
When the design for Chando was originally made, she was only a long-haired girl and there was no rose in character design. Somewhere along the line, they added a red rose and went with that for a while, until in 2022 when she decided to look into blue roses and their message, so she decided to use it as a motif, near her heart.[27]
Her thoughts on Usseewa becoming a hit in 2020 was that it doesn't feel real yet, and that it's like someone else's thing.[12]
Her favourite line in Usseewa is "Ah tsumaranee, nankai kikaseru nda sono memorii?" (嗚呼つまらねぇ 何回聞かせるんだそのメモリー, "Ah, so boring. How many times do I have to listen to those memories of yours?").[12]
When she recorded Usseewa, it was done in a studio.[12] It is similar to recording in a closet, where she puts her computer on at a desk, records and sings alone. Sometimes, an engineer accompanies her, but she likes to rerecord until she's satisfied so she wouldn't force anyone to stay, and even if they agreed she'd still be concerned. Therefore, she settled on a style similar to when she was recording in a closet, where she goes in and comes out when she wants to take a break.[3]
